title.purpose: Current book title, section titles, and major controls.

label.purpose: Metadata, secondary controls, and compact navigation.

motion.name: state-transition
motion.purpose: Use only for hover, focus, collapse, and mode changes.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: A quiet primary action for selecting a folder or confirming a rare task.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { min-height: 34px; padding: 0 14px; border: 1px solid #8da101; border-radius: 6px; background: transparent; color: #5c6a72; font: 500 14px/1.4 Lato, system-ui, sans-serif; transition: background-color 180ms ease-out, border-color 180ms ease-out; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #e5e6c5; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #8da101; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Reading Body
components.html: Readable body text stays central while controls step back.
components.css: .ds-reading-body { max-width: 72ch; padding: 120px 24px; border-radius: 8px; background: #f3ead3; color: #5c6a72; font: 400 16px/1.8 Lato, system-ui, sans-serif; }

components.name: Chrome Panel
components.description: A restrained support panel for files, outline, or settings.
components.css: .ds-chrome-panel { padding: 16px; border: 1px solid #ddd8be; border-radius: 6px; background: #f3ead3; color: #5c6a72; font-family: Lato, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-panel-title { margin-bottom: 12px; font-size: 16px; font-weight: 600; } .ds-panel-item { width: 100%; padding: 8px 10px; border: 0; border-radius: 6px; background: transparent; color: inherit; text-align: left; } .ds-panel-item:hover, .ds-panel-item:focus-visible { background: #e5e6c5; outline: none; }

narrative.overview: The interface exists to protect the act of reading. It should feel low-profile, lightweight, and eye-friendly, with chrome that appears only to orient the user and then steps back. The strongest visual signal is the body text; everything else is supporting structure.
keyCharacteristics: Discreet application chrome around a calm reading surface.
Restrained color, used for actions and current state instead of decoration.
Dense enough for desktop utility, quiet enough for long reading sessions.
Transparent mode as the lightest state: readable floating text with minimal surrounding UI.

rules.name: The Ten Percent Accent Rule
rules.body: Accent color is reserved for primary action, active state, and focus. If the page starts to look green or purple, the accent is overused.

rules.name: The Transparent Means Lighter Rule
rules.body: Transparent mode should remove chrome before it removes legibility. Body text contrast must remain readable even when panels vanish.

rules.name: The Body Text Wins Rule
rules.body: When a component competes visually with the novel text, reduce the component before reducing the text.

rules.name: The No Decorative Glass Rule
rules.body: Blur and translucent panels are allowed only to keep floating text or controls readable. They are not a default card style.

dos: Do keep the product register: familiar desktop tool patterns, restrained motion, and predictable controls.
Do make transparent mode the lightest UI state, with floating readable body text as the priority.
Do remove or redesign existing structures when they do not serve reading, including the current half-collapsed outline pattern.
Do keep accent color rare and meaningful.
Do verify contrast for body text in light, dark, and transparent contexts.
donts: Don't make this feel like a complex library-management app.
Don't make it feel like a commercial reading platform, storefront, or recommendation product.
Don't preserve current rough layout decisions as design requirements.
Don't add decorative gradients, glass cards, heavy shadows, or large rounded cards.
Don't let file management, chapter controls, or settings compete with the reading body.
